Operating Characteristics of the gBOIN-ET Design

Source: R/sim_gboin_et.R
sim_gboin_et.Rd

Simulate trials of the gBOIN-ET design of Takeda, Morita and Taguri (2022) under one scenario of probabilities of toxicity and efficacy categories, select the optimal biological dose (OBD) of each trial, and summarize how often each dose is selected and how many patients are treated at each dose, with their total scores.

Usage

sim_gboin_et(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_grade,
  p_resp_grade,
  score,
  score_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  lambda1 = NULL,
  lambda2 = NULL,
  eta1 = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  est_method = c("observed", "fp_linear", "fp_logistic"),
  obd_method = c("max_resp", "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear",
    "utility_scoring"),
  min_obd_sample = 1,
  w1 = 0.33,
  w2 = 1.09,
  t_low = NULL,
  t_upp = NULL,
  e_low = NULL,
  e_upp = NULL,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.47 / 1.5 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized efficacy score, for example 0.95 / 1.5 for a target equivalent efficacy score of 0.95 with a largest score of 1.5.

p_grade

Numeric matrix. True probability of each toxicity category (rows) at each dose (columns, in increasing dose order). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without a toxicity event.

p_resp_grade

Numeric matrix with one column per dose. True probability of each efficacy category (rows). Every column sums to 1. The first row is the category without an efficacy event.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

score_resp

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_resp_grade. Score of each efficacy category, for example c(0, 1, 1.5) for stable or progressive disease, partial response and complete response. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at any dose. Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size, which is the default of the 'boinet' package.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

Numeric scalars or NULL. Boundaries of the mean toxicity score and of the mean efficacy score. Defaults to NULL, the boundaries of boin_et_boundary for the targets. Give all three to use other values, such as those printed in an article.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the toxicity event and the efficacy event of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly. Defaults to FALSE, which keeps to Takeda et al. (2018), who do not allow dose skipping during escalation; see Details.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimator of the mean efficacy scores: "observed" (the default) for the observed means, "fp_linear" for the linear fractional polynomial of Takeda et al. (2022), or "fp_logistic" for the fractional polynomial logistic regression of the 'boinet' package, which needs the 'mfp' package.

obd_method

Character scalar. Selection rule: "max_resp" (the default) for the admissible dose with the highest estimated response rate up to the estimated MTD, or the dose that maximizes the utility "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear" or "utility_scoring" among the admissible doses.

min_obd_sample

Integer scalar. Only doses given to at least this many patients can be selected. Defaults to 1. The simulations of Takeda et al. (2022) use 6.

w1, w2

Numeric scalars. Weights of the weighted utility q - w1 * p - w2 * p * (p > p_tox), where p and q are the estimated DLT and response rates. Default to 0.33 and 1.09.

t_low, t_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. DLT rates between which the truncated linear utility falls from one to zero. Default to p_saf and p_tox.

e_low, e_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. Response rates between which the truncated linear utility rises from zero to one. Default to p_saf_resp / 2 and target_resp.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of the scoring utility for a patient with neither DLT nor response and for a patient with both, the scores of a response without DLT and of a DLT without response being 100 and 0. Default to 40 and 60.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials and the selected OBDs in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress with messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_et_oc, which is a list with components

design

"gBOIN-ET".

target, target_resp

The targets of the mean normalized scores.

p_true, p_resp

The true mean normalized toxicity and efficacy scores of the doses.

n_doses, n_trials

Numbers of doses and of simulated trials.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

The boundaries.

sel_percent

Percentage of trials selecting each dose as the OBD.

percent_no_obd

Percentage of trials selecting no OBD.

percent_early_stop

Percentage of trials stopped early.

n_pts_dose, n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Average numbers of patients and average totals of the normalized toxicity and efficacy scores at each dose.

total_n_pts, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their averages per trial.

n_grade_dose, n_resp_grade_dose

Average numbers of patients of each toxicity category and of each efficacy category (rows) at each dose (columns).

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials ending for each reason, see boin_et_simulate.

est_method, obd_method

The OBD selection used.

settings

List of the design parameters.

call

The matched call.

trials, obd

The simulated trials and the selected OBDs, when keep_trials is TRUE.

Details

The trials are simulated by gboin_et_simulate and the OBD is selected by gboin_et_select_obd; see there for the rules. The result prints like that of sim_boin_et, with scores in the place of DLTs and responses, and enters oc_results and oc_compare under the name gBOIN-ET.

The simulations of Takeda et al. (2022) estimate the efficacy scores by the linear fractional polynomial (est_method = "fp_linear") and select the OBD among the doses with at least six patients (min_obd_sample = 6). Their program does not draw the categories from the probabilities of their Table S1: it draws one Bernoulli variate for each category and takes the highest category that comes up, so that the probabilities of the lower categories are smaller than tabulated. inst/reproduce/reproduce_Takeda2022.R gives the probabilities that the program draws and compares the results with Table 1 of the article.

References

Takeda, K., Morita, S. and Taguri, M. (2022). gBOIN-ET: The generalized Bayesian optimal interval design for optimal dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity in early clinical trials. Biometrical Journal, 64(7), 1178-1191. doi:10.1002/bimj.202100263

See also

sim_gboin_et_multi, gboin_et_simulate, gboin_et_select_obd, sim_boin_et

Examples

# Toxicity grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4, and stable or progressive disease,
# partial response and complete response, at four doses
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.83, 0.62, 0.51, 0.34),
  c(0.12, 0.18, 0.19, 0.16),
  c(0.04, 0.11, 0.14, 0.15),
  c(0.01, 0.09, 0.16, 0.35)
)
p_resp_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.90, 0.50, 0.30, 0.25),
  c(0.05, 0.35, 0.20, 0.20),
  c(0.05, 0.15, 0.50, 0.55)
)
oc <- sim_gboin_et(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 0.95 / 1.5,
  p_grade = p_grade, p_resp_grade = p_resp_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), score_resp = c(0, 1, 1.5),
  n_cohort = 10, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 1000, seed = 123
)
oc
#> gBOIN-ET operating characteristics
#>   target toxicity score: 0.3133333
#>   target efficacy score: 0.6333333
#>   trials               : 1000
#>   cohorts              : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 30
#>   lambda1 / lambda2    : 0.1413 / 0.3733
#>   eta1                 : 0.5
#>   OBD selection        : max_resp with observed efficacy scores
#> 
#>                         DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4 Total / No OBD
#> True toxicity score (%) 7.7 22.3 31.7 50.3               
#> True efficacy score (%) 8.3 38.3 63.3 68.3               
#> OBD selected (%)        2.0 31.4 59.3  2.8            4.5
#> Patients treated        4.4 10.6 13.3  1.3           29.5
#> Toxicity score          0.3  2.3  4.3  0.7            7.6
#> Efficacy score          0.4  4.1  8.4  0.9           13.8
#> 
#> Trials stopped early: 4.5%

# The same trials with the OBD selection of the article
sim_gboin_et(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 0.95 / 1.5,
  p_grade = p_grade, p_resp_grade = p_resp_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5), score_resp = c(0, 1, 1.5),
  n_cohort = 10, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 1000,
  est_method = "fp_linear", min_obd_sample = 6, seed = 123
)$sel_percent
#>  DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4 
#>  0.7 31.3 60.6  2.1
